title: UNCO SA 13.11.2026 – Fixed assets and depreciation

questions.text: An iPad commissioned on 2 October 2026 costs €1,200 net with full input VAT deduction. Its useful life is ten years. What is 2026 depreciation under the tax half-year convention?
What is the iPad carrying amount on 31 December 2026 with €1,200 cost and €60 depreciation?
A dishwasher costing €1,160 has annual depreciation of €145 and was commissioned on 18 May 2023. The asset-register exercise specifies eight months. What is 2023 depreciation?
The same dishwasher was commissioned on 18 May and has annual depreciation of €145. What depreciation applies instead under the tax half-year convention?
Depreciation reduces profit but does not cause another payment.
Which entry records €60 straight-line depreciation on equipment capitalised in account 0620?
Which statement describes the textbook low-value asset limit?
options: Any value if the item is paid for in cash
Acquisition cost up to €1,000 excluding deductible VAT and independently usable
Sale price up to €1,000 including all VAT
questions.correctAnswer: Acquisition cost up to €1,000 excluding deductible VAT and independently usable

questions.text: A computer, monitor and printer together cost €629 gross or €524.17 net. Individual prices are missing. What must be assumed for an immediate write-off as one low-value unit?
options: None of the VAT is deductible
One eligible low-value unit and deductible input VAT
Each item demonstrably costs exactly €209.67 gross
None of the items may be used for business
questions.correctAnswer: One eligible low-value unit and deductible input VAT

questions.text: The eight-month asset-register example and the tax half-year convention give the same dishwasher depreciation.

Equipment costs €1,200 net, is capitalised and commissioned on 2 October 2026, and has a ten-year useful life. Input VAT is fully deductible. Using the tax half-year convention, calculate the rate, full-year depreciation, 2026 depreciation and carrying amount on 31 December.
questions.correctAnswer: 10%; €1,200 / 10 = €120 per year; second-half commissioning gives €60 in 2026; carrying amount €1,200 − €60 = €1,140.
